messages.subject: Giving back to ggplot2
parts:
Hi everyone,

From time to time people contact me asking how they can give back to
ggplot2. I thought I'd aggregate the possibilities here and publicise
them, just in case you're in a giving mode ;)

* Cite ggplot2!
Cost: zero. Effort: low

The easiest way to support ggplot2 is to remember to cite it
when you publish your work. You can get the citation by running
citation("ggplot2") in R.

* Write a letter to my department chair.
Cost: zero. Effort: medium

It helps to let my department know directly that you're finding
my work useful. The easiest way to do that would be to send a letter
to my chair, Kathy Ensor, at the address below.

Kathy Ensor
Professor and Chair of Statistics
Department of Statistics, MS 138
Rice University
P.O. Box 1892
Houston, TX 77251-1892

* Buy me something off my amazon wish list.
Cost: low. Effort: low.

I love getting packages ;)
http://amazon.com/gp/registry/1Y65N3VFA613B

* Host an intern
Cost: medium. Effort: medium.

Would you like to have a talented Rice grad or undergrad work with
your over summer? I often have students looking for summer work.
Let me know if you're interested.

* Fund a grad student.
Cost: high. Effort: high

If you have $40,000 lying around and you'd like to get some
significant research done, you could hire a grad student for a
year or two. It may also be possible to combine your funds with
NSF grant money to reduce the cost.

Thanks!

Hadley

--
Assistant Professor / Dobelman Family Junior Chair
Department of Statistics / Rice University
http://had.co.nz/
